text: Test every outside-service call with a recorded fixture and a simulated quota or rate-limit error. Quota errors from speech and weather services appeared in past projects; the code must switch source or write a NEEDS_YOU item, not fail silently.
Cache outside-service responses on disk, keyed by the request, and read from the cache in tests and re-runs. It saves quota and makes runs repeatable.
Every number and chart in a report comes from one script that rebuilds it from raw input. Deliver the script with the report and re-run it clean before delivery.
Recompute each headline number a second way (for example a loop against a grouped query) and compare. A mismatch is a defect to explain, not a rounding note.
Profile input before analysis: row counts, date ranges, duplicates, missing values, units. Put the results in the report so the reader can judge the data.

Process large data through scripts, never by pasting it into the conversation. In Anthropic's test a 1,862-row table pasted into a prompt scored 7 of 25; queried through code it scored 25 of 25 at a fraction of the cost.
Run a small sample (one lesson, one page, one region) and show it to the owner before a full or paid run. It catches a wrong voice, format or source cheaply.
Put each outside data source behind a small interface, so a second source can replace it when one fails, changes price or runs out of quota.

Ask for API keys through the secure credential form, or add a NEEDS_YOU item with the clicks to store the key in the environment's settings. Never write a key into a file, commit, log or reply; if one is pasted in chat, do not repeat it and suggest rotating it. Keys were pasted into chat three times in past projects.
Long harvests write results to disk as they go and can resume from the last saved point, so a rate limit or a session end costs minutes, not the run.

Keep claims within what the data supports: no correlation stated as cause, sample sizes shown, and no figure that misleads (a raw count where a rate is what matters). The owner has rejected a misleading count before.
Record random seeds, source versions and the date of each data pull, so a later re-run can be compared with the first.
